about: The lesser doxology — the short praise of the Trinity with which the Church has ended the psalms and canticles of the Office since antiquity. At Mass it stands in the Iúdica psalm, at the Introit's psalm and at the Lavábo. Its Latin form with the added clause “Sicut erat in princípio” — a confession that the Son is eternal — was ordered in Gaul by the Council of Vaison (529), expressly against the Arians. The clause was framed of the Son, and is read today of the glory. The synod believed the East used the clause too — mistakenly: the East to this day sings the doxology without it, and “Sicut erat…” remained a peculiarity of the Latin West.

s01.translation: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

s02.translation: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

w002.function: Glory to whom — to the Father. The first of three datives of the Trinity.

w007.function: Agrees with “Spirítui” (w006). The adjective keeps its own declension — hence “Sancto”, not “Sanctui”.

w009.function: Continuing state in the past. The understood subject is the glory.

w017.function: With the accusative — the time toward which it runs: “unto the ages”. Compare “in” (w010) with the ablative — a point in time.

w018.function: The time toward which it runs, after “in” (w017).

w019.function: Genitive with “sǽcula” (w018): ages of ages — like “Holy of Holies”.
